instructions: Set a 10 inch cast iron or other ovenproof skillet on the middle rack and heat the oven to 425°F with the pan inside. Take the 4 eggs and the 1/2 cup milk out of the fridge while it heats.

Put the eggs, milk, 2/3 cup flour, 4 tsp sugar, 1 1/4 tsp vanilla and the pinch of salt in a blender. Blend for about 20 seconds, until smooth with no lumps. No blender? Whisk the eggs and milk hard in a bowl, then whisk in the rest until smooth.
Once the oven is fully hot, take the skillet out with an oven mitt and set it on the stove. Add the 3 tbsp butter and swirl until it melts and coats the bottom and sides.
Pour in the batter all at once and put the pan straight back in the oven.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until it's puffed high at the edges and deep golden. Don't open the oven while it bakes.
Take it out and set the skillet on a heatproof surface. It'll sink a little as it cools. Scatter the blueberries over the middle and dust it with 1 tbsp of the powdered sugar through a small sieve.
Cut it into 4 wedges and serve right away with the maple syrup.
method_notes: All three heat the empty skillet in the oven, blend eggs, flour, milk, a little sugar, vanilla and salt, melt butter in the hot pan and bake the batter until it puffs, without opening the oven. Spend With Pennies (the lead) uses 3 eggs to 1/2 cup flour and 1/3 cup milk at 425°F for 15 to 18 minutes and serves two; Once Upon a Chef uses nearly the same batter at 400°F as a serving for four, and Plated Cravings makes a 4 egg, 1 cup flour version in the same 10 inch pan. This scales the lead up to 4 eggs so one pancake in a 10 inch skillet feeds four, and tops it with the berries, powdered sugar and maple syrup the sources serve it with.
